description:
Metadata for one embedding. The vector itself lives in the index; this is
the record that makes the index auditable and erasable.

`memory_id` is deliberately the same identifier used by the graph node. §5.4
requires it: "store vectors under the same stable memory identifier used in
the graph". Any code that generates a separate vector id is a bug — it makes
deletion propagation unprovable.

memory_id.description: Identical to the graph fact's id. Not a separate vector id.
memory_id.title: Memory Id

subject_id.description: Owning subject, so the index can be filtered before similarity search
subject_id.title: Subject Id

embedding_model_version.description: Pinned version of that model. A change here invalidates every vector it produced.
embedding_model_version.title: Embedding Model Version

vector_dimension.description: Length of the stored vector; must match the index
vector_dimension.title: Vector Dimension

approved_text_fields.description: Exactly which fields of the memory were embedded, e.g. ['fact_text']. §5.4: 'Generate embeddings only for approved memory fields.'
approved_text_fields.title: Approved Text Fields

text_field_version.description: Version of the text-assembly rule used to build the embedded string. Changing how the text is composed must invalidate old vectors even when the model is unchanged.
text_field_version.title: Text Field Version

source_text_hash.description: Hash of the exact embedded string, so a stale vector can be detected without re-embedding
source_text_hash.title: Source Text Hash

deletion_status.description: 'pending_deletion' is set the moment a deletion job starts, so retrieval stops using the vector before the index write completes. Prevents a deleted memory surfacing during propagation.
deletion_status.title: Deletion Status

policy_approved.description: A vector may only exist for a policy-approved fact (§7.2 step 6). Recorded for audit.
policy_approved.title: Policy Approved

title: VectorRecord
